newsitem.title: HONG KONG: European stock markets seen strong in 1997 - Invesco.
newsitem.headline: European stock markets seen strong in 1997 - Invesco.

text.p: European equity markets will put in a strong performance in 1997, boosted by a winning combination of tight fiscal policy and relaxed monetary policy, fund manager Invesco said on Monday.
"In Europe, we have a whole set of factors that are positive for stock markets," Rory Powe, Invesco's head of European equities, said.

While the European Monetary Union (EMU) was constraining the growth of many economies, a benign inflation rate environment and a new emphasis on creating shareholder value would support equities throughout the coming year, Powe said.

Trading at between 15 and 18 times 1996 earnings, European equities represented good value for pension funds under pressure to meet future liabilities, particularly in a declining rate environment generating poor returns on fixed income instruments.
Swiss pension funds with 300 billion Swiss francs under management had only 15 percent of their portfolios invested in equities, Powe said.
"Domestic liquidity is going into equities," he said.
A difficult economic environment had forced companies in Europe to be more resourceful and to seek greater efficiencies, Invesco said.
In Germany, companies were creating shareholder value by returning to their core business, spinning off non-core assets, making acquisitions and considering share buybacks.
Invesco favoured growth stocks, particularly global winners and niche players with pricing power, with a minimum exposure of 50 percent in all its European portfolios.
Cyclical and financial stocks were being bought only at valuation extremes, Powe said.

Stocks favoured by Invesco, a bottom-up investor, include Fresenius and Disetronic Medical Systems Inc in the health care sector, Gucci and Bulgari in the luxury goods sector, Sodexho and Tomra in the service sector and Getronics, Ericsson and Baan in the technology sector.
